conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Domino Run
style.description: A domino rally on a polished wooden floor seen low and close: hundreds of glossy plain-faced coloured tiles standing in curving lines, spirals and branching paths, up a little stair and across a plank bridge, in warm window daylight with soft floor reflections. A topple wave runs every path at a set speed; each tile's fall is a closed-form function of time that comes to rest leaning on the next; one tile splits a line in two, lines trip gadgets (a ball rolls, a flag pops up, a banner drops), and a two-colour field topples row by row to reveal a picture or word. The camera chases the wave front.

map.description: honey oak planks, 0.48 m boards running along x

motion: Topple: each tile rotates about its front bottom edge; angle = closed-form accelerating fall from its trigger time, clamped by the contact with the next tile, so it comes to rest leaning on it (~75 deg on a straight run).
Wave: trigger times come from the wave speed along each path (0.16 s per tile at the defaults); the last tile of a line falls flat.
Split / merge: one tile strikes two side-by-side tiles that curve apart; a merge tile falls at the first arrival.
Stair / bridge: tiles step up one block at a time, run across a plank bridge and step down; a tile before a step leans on the step edge.
Field: a grid of two-colour tiles topples row by row (or in a vee from the entry tile) and the backs show a picture or word.
Gadgets: a rolling ball starts or relays the chain (closed-form deceleration), a flag springs up, a banner drops.
Camera: chases the wave front, low and close, then lifts into a wide that fills the frame with the finished field.

notes.mechanism: rally.js plans every tile: trigger = earliest arrival of the topple wave over the trigger graph (lines, a split, a ball, a field fan); fall angle = closed form of (t - trigger) clamped by the exact corner-on-face contact with the next tile.
